climate: Summers are close to rainless. Vines need irrigation or deep soil that stores winter rain, but disease is rare.
Rain picks up at harvest. Growers race to pick before rot sets in, and vintages vary more.

soil.rock: Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water. Sand is warm and airy. It drains fast but holds little water, and phylloxera does not thrive in it. River deposits are a mix of gravel, sand and silt. They are often fertile, so vines can grow vigorously.
